## Natural history notes

A medium-sized orange butterfly characterized by its scalloped wings, dark checkered markings, and pale silvery-white spots on the underside of the hindwings. In Florida, it is found in sunny open habitats such as fields, prairies, roadsides, gardens, parks, pine flatwoods, and disturbed areas where violets, passionflowers, and other host plants grow. Adults feed on nectar from many wildflowers, while the caterpillars feed on violets, passionflowers, purslane, and related low plants, often using open weedy vegetation for shelter and development.
